items.title: Name, tagline and the promise
items.body: The product is written Moksy in prose: capital M, never MOKSY or moksy. The one tagline is "Turn your idea into a build-ready plan." The one-line description of how it works is "Idea in, build-ready plan out. AI structures it, vetted experts refine it." Three older taglines are retired from the interface: "Empowering your digital transformation", "Building Future-Ready Brands" and "AI requirements + expert review". The home headline stays "Bring your idea to life". The document Moksy produces is called a Blueprint; "build-ready plan" is its plain-English twin, which is why the tagline did not change when the document was named. Moksy is the voice that asks the questions: where the platform speaks it says "Moksy will ask…" or "Tell Moksy…". Source: brand guidelines (18 Aug 2026) and Moksy Lexicon (2 Sep 2026).

items.title: The spine and the six marks
items.body: Five words, in order, carry the whole journey: Idea, Briefing, Blueprint, Review, Build. It is the tagline made concrete. Moksy owns six capitalised marks and keeps them rare on purpose, because every coined word is a word a new customer must learn: Moksy, MOX, MXP, Blueprint, Briefing and Ladder. Spec Sprint is also a proper noun: the one-day, human-led engagement, always two capitalised words, never split. Every mark has a plain-English twin that is shown on first use on a page, for example MOX (Moksy credit). Source: Moksy Lexicon part B (2 Sep 2026).

items.title: Words for the customer journey
items.body: Idea is what you type in. Briefing is the guided conversation where Moksy learns your idea; it replaces interview, conversation, Q&A and AI requirements. Brief is the answers your Briefing has gathered, as a noun. Blueprint is your build-ready plan; it replaces report, plan (as the document), spec, solution plan, document and blueprint variants. Areas are the analysis areas a Blueprint covers, 22 in a complete one; the word replaces pillars everywhere a customer or reviewer can read it. A Section is one rendered part of a Blueprint. Build is the stage after the Blueprint: exports, hiring, tools. The nav word Exports replaces Downloads. Source: Moksy Lexicon C1 (2 Sep 2026).

items.title: Reviews and who does them
items.body: Review is one noun with three kinds, each a single adjective. Peer Review is free, from the community. Expert Review is included in Pro and Max and done by an accredited reviewer. Priority Review is paid and fast: an Expert Review within 36 hours. Priority won over Rush because it is already the on-screen badge and says what you buy, a place at the front. A review of one part of a Blueprint is a Section Review. The tabs on the Reviews page are Peer, Expert, Priority and History. Retired labels include Community review (now Peer Review) and Urgent expert review (now Priority Review). Source: Moksy Lexicon C1 and C9 (2 Sep 2026).

questions.answer: A Priority Review is an Expert Review with a clock on it: an accredited reviewer checks your Blueprint within 36 hours. It is paid, so you get a place at the front of the queue. If you would rather not pay, a Peer Review is free, and Expert Reviews are included in Pro and Max.
questions.rubric: A good answer: says a Priority Review is a paid Expert Review done within 36 hours by an accredited reviewer; refers to the document as a Blueprint; uses the Review names (Peer, Expert, Priority) correctly; if MOX is mentioned it appears upper-case with its plain twin (Moksy credit) on first use; sounds friendly, professional and confident in plain language; uses British spelling; roughly 60 words. Penalise: calling it urgent or rush review, report/spec, jargon such as engine or pillars.

items.title: Money and membership words
items.body: MOX is Moksy credit; 1 MOX equals $0.01. It is always upper-case, with the plain twin on first use per page, and never written mox or Mox. MXP is Moksy Experience Points: the letters, upper-case, never XP, points or score. They are one transposition apart and sit side by side on the reviewer's Desk, so always pair a unit with its noun: Wallet · 1,200 MOX, Ladder · 340 MXP. Wallet is where MOX lives (not MOX wallet). A Pack is a one-off MOX purchase. Starter is the free MOX granted on joining. Escrow is MOX held while a Review is open, held until you accept the review. Membership is the monthly plan; customer names are Free, Pro and Max, with Team as the label for an organisation. The reviewer's monthly plan is Reviewer Membership: Reviewer, Reviewer Pro, Reviewer Elite. Earnings is MOX a reviewer has earned; Payouts is money sent to a bank. Tip is MOX sent to a reviewer beyond the fee. Spec Sprint requests live under Sprints, never called concierge on a customer surface. Source: Moksy Lexicon C3, C4 and B3 (2 Sep 2026).

items.title: Colour and logo
items.body: One accent, a dark ink and neutrals. Primary brand colour is Moksy orange-red #EF4123; secondary is deep petrol #002835; accent grey is #6D6E71; text ink is #0F172A; the page canvas is #FAFBFC and surfaces are white. Brand orange is the only non-neutral colour used for actions, with one primary action per view; it is never replaced by black, blue, indigo or grey for a primary action. Status colours are emerald for success, amber for warning, rose for danger and indigo for info, used for data and state only, never as page fills. Logo files are local (horizontal and vertical master logos and an icon master); never link a remote moksy.ai URL as a fallback. Logo height is h-8 in headers and footers and h-10 on sign-in pages, with h-6 or h-7 for the compact icon mark. A decorative logo has empty alt text and aria-hidden; a meaningful image has descriptive alt text; an avatar's alt text is the person's name. Imagery is minimal and icon-led, with product and data visuals preferred over stock photography. Source: brand guidelines sections 2 and 4 (18 Aug 2026).

questions.prompt: A colleague proposes a campaign graphic with a blue Buy Now button, a stock photo of a handshake and the slogan "EMPOWERING YOUR DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION" in capitals. List what you would change and why.
questions.answer: Make the primary button Moksy orange (#EF4123), because brand orange is the only action colour. Replace the stock photo with a minimal, icon-led or product visual. Replace the retired tagline with "Turn your idea into a build-ready plan." Remove the all-capitals: ALL-CAPS is only for the eyebrow style. Use Title Case on the button and a short verb such as Start.
questions.rubric: A good answer names at least four of: primary action must be brand orange not blue; imagery should be minimal icon-led or product/data not stock photography; the slogan is a retired tagline and should be "Turn your idea into a build-ready plan."; ALL-CAPS is only allowed through the eyebrow style; Title Case and a short verb for the button (Buy is not on the approved list; Start free is the primary call to action); one primary action per view. Give credit for each correct change with its reason.

items.title: Typography and casing
items.body: Headings use Bebas Neue (decided by the founder 18 Aug 2026; the font file still has to be added, until then headings render in the system font). Body text is Myriad Variable and code and ids use JetBrains Mono. The type scale is expressed as roles: display (marketing hero only), headline (one page title per screen), subheadline (section heading), title (card heading), eyebrow (a small micro-label and the only sanctioned ALL-CAPS), lead, paragraph and small. The maximum weight is semibold. Casing: headings, buttons, navigation, tabs and labels use Title Case; body copy, descriptions, help text, empty-state messages and tooltips use sentence case; proper nouns stay as written. Buttons are one verb where possible, with a verb-first label. Empty states read "No {things} yet." with the trailing full stop, for example "No Blueprints yet." Source: brand guidelines sections 3 and 6 and Lexicon C9 (2 Sep 2026).

items.title: Voice, tone and spelling
items.body: Moksy's personality is friendly, professional and confident, in plain language that never adds guesswork. Spelling is British English everywhere a person reads: organise, colour, analyse, centre, behaviour, judgement, cancelled, catalogue, artefact, grey, towards; licence as a noun and license as a verb; programme for a scheme but program for software. Code identifiers, enum values, HTTP header names and CSS keep their original spelling. Customer and reviewer surfaces use the lexicon words. Operator surfaces may keep internal names such as pillars, Newton, Base and Master or Patterns, but those names never appear on a customer or reviewer surface, in an email or in a generated document. Words that name people never use Ninja, Guru, Mystic, Sage or Master as titles, so they read the same in every country. A register split between terse admin copy and warmer customer copy is allowed, but it must be deliberate. Source: brand guidelines section 6 and Lexicon B3 (2 Sep 2026).

items.title: People and the Ladder
items.body: Persona homes are Home for the customer, Desk for the reviewer and Console for staff. The people words are Guest (not signed in), Member (signed in, on Free), Customer (anyone with a Project), Reviewer (accredited) and Staff (operator). The only customer standing words are Guest, Member, Pro and Max. Moksy is the platform as an actor, in first person; never the system, the engine, Newton or Moksy AI on a customer surface. The reviewer Ladder has six named rungs, with numeric levels beneath: Candidate, Contributor, Reviewer, Senior, Principal and Fellow, written as, for example, Senior · Level 9. The twenty fantasy titles (Novice to Titan) and the five tier names (Foundation to Apex) are retired from every Moksy surface. A Standing is where a reviewer is now: rung, band and tracks. Band is how demanding a piece of work is (C1 to C4). Calibration is the blind test with seeded defects. Accreditation is the whole route to Reviewer. Source: Moksy Lexicon C2, C4 to C6 (2 Sep 2026).

questions.prompt: Rewrite these three email subject lines to follow Moksy's formula: (1) "Your Moksy report!!" (2) "500 pillars added to your moksy account" (3) "Moksy Notification". Explain the rule you applied.
questions.answer: (1) Your Blueprint is ready. (2) 500 areas added to your Moksy account. (3) Moksy update. The rule is {Thing} plus {state}, with Title Case on the mark, sentence case otherwise, Moksy always capitalised, and the lexicon words (Blueprint, Areas) instead of report and pillars.
questions.rubric: A good answer gives: (1) Your Blueprint is ready (state included, no exclamation marks, Blueprint not report); (2) 500 areas added to your Moksy account (Areas not pillars; capital M); (3) Moksy update. It also states the {Thing} + {state} formula or equivalent. Partial credit for getting two of three or for naming the rule without correct rewrites.

items.title: Emails, buttons and navigation
items.body: Email subjects follow the formula {Thing} + {state}, with Title Case on the mark and sentence case otherwise, and Moksy always capitalised: "Your Blueprint is ready", "{n} areas added to your Moksy account", "You can now claim Expert Reviews", "Review my Blueprint: {name}" and the generic "Moksy update" (not "Moksy Notification"). Buttons are one verb with one glyph per verb: Start, Continue, Claim, Export, Share, Review and Top up (the one two-word verb). There is one primary call to action everywhere, "Start free"; "Get my Blueprint" is used on the home form only. Customer navigation is one word each: Home, Projects, Briefing, Blueprint, Reviews, Exports, Messages, Wallet, Membership, Areas, Sprints, Profile. Reviewer navigation: Desk, Queue, Standing, Ladder, Earnings, Payouts, Membership, Directory, Accreditation, Availability. Source: Moksy Lexicon C8 and C9 (2 Sep 2026).
